mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 6.0% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and corporate costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 1% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -4%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL (core inflation) above 0.2 percentage points in the same month signals a disinflationary tightening, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by >0.2pp in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A positive year-over-year change in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 combined with an unemployment rate above 8% signals a labor market recovery in a deep recession, which boosts investor confidence and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above 5% for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change > 5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in Real Personal Income (proxied by GDPC1 growth) below -0.5% combined with a concurrent rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% signals stagflation, which erodes purchasing power and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
